rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: An aqueous solution ‘A’ turns phenolphthalein solution pink. When another aqueous solution ‘B’ is added to the pink solution, the pink colour disappears. Now when a few drops of solution ‘A’ are added to this reaction, the mixture appears pink again. The respective changes in the nature of the solution are from :
rows.solution:
Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic and neutral solutions and pink in basic solutions. Solution A turns it pink, so A is basic.

Adding solution B removes the pink colour: B neutralises the base, and with enough of it the mixture becomes acidic. Adding a few drops of A again makes the mixture pink, so it is basic once more.

So the nature changes from basic to acidic to basic. This is option (D) basic \(\rightarrow\) acidic \(\rightarrow\) basic.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Green plants trap only 1% of the energy of sunlight that falls on their leaves.

**Reason (R) :** All green plants are the producers in a food chain.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Green plants capture only about 1% of the energy of the sunlight that falls on their leaves and convert it into food energy, so the Assertion is true. All green plants make their own food by photosynthesis, so they are the producers in a food chain, and the Reason is also true.

But the Reason only says that green plants are producers; it does not explain why they trap so small a fraction of the sunlight. Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.stem: Write the formula and the molecular mass of the third homologue of alcohols. State how the boiling point of an alcohol changes as one moves from lower to higher homologues.
rows.solution:
The first three members of the alcohol series are methanol, \(\mathrm{CH_3OH}\), ethanol, \(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}\), and propanol, \(\mathrm{C_3H_7OH}\). So the third homologue is propanol, \(\mathrm{C_3H_7OH}\).

Molecular mass \(= 3 \times 12 + 7 \times 1 + 16 + 1 = 60\) u.

The boiling point of alcohols increases as one moves from lower to higher homologues, since the molecular mass increases.

rows.stem: Identify the organ in the human female reproductive system where the sperm encounters the egg cell. What will happen if it is blocked ? Name the technique by which it can be blocked.
rows.solution:
The sperm encounters the egg cell in the fallopian tube (oviduct).

If the fallopian tube is blocked, the egg cannot reach the sperm, so fertilisation will not take place.

It can be blocked by surgery: the technique is called tubectomy.

rows.stem:
“The linear magnification produced by a spherical mirror is \(+3\).” Based on this statement answer the following questions :

(a) What is the type of mirror ?

(b) Where is the object located ?

(c) List two properties of the image formed (other than the size/magnification).
rows.solution:
(a) A positive magnification means the image is erect, and a magnification of \(+3\) means it is three times the size of the object. A convex mirror always forms a diminished image, so a magnified erect image can only come from a concave (converging) mirror.

(b) A concave mirror forms an enlarged, erect image only when the object is between the pole and the principal focus.

(c) Any two: the image is virtual; it is erect; it is formed behind the mirror.

rows.stem: The filament of an electric lamp draws a current of \(0{\cdot}5\) A, which lights for 2 hours. Calculate the charge that flows through the circuit.
rows.solution:
Current \(I = 0{\cdot}5\) A and time \(t = 2\) hours \(= 2 \times 3600 = 7200\) s.

Since \(I = \dfrac{Q}{t}\),

\(Q = I \times t = 0{\cdot}5 \times 2 \times 3600 = 3600\) C.

A charge of 3600 C flows through the circuit.

rows.stem:
Answer the following questions in the context of electrolysis of water :

(a) Why is this reaction/process called a decomposition reaction ?

(b) Giving reason state whether this reaction is exothermic or endothermic.

(c) Name the gases collected at the anode and cathode.

(d) What is the mass ratio of the gases collected at the anode and cathode ?
rows.solution:
In the electrolysis of water, an electric current is passed through water (with a few drops of dilute sulphuric acid added):

\(\mathrm{2H_2O(l) \xrightarrow{\text{electricity}} 2H_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

(a) A single substance, water, breaks up into two simpler substances, hydrogen gas and oxygen gas, so it is a decomposition reaction.

(b) It is endothermic: electrical energy has to be supplied continuously to decompose the water, so energy is absorbed in the reaction.

(c) Oxygen is collected at the anode and hydrogen at the cathode.

(d) The equation gives 1 mole of oxygen (32 g) for every 2 moles of hydrogen (\(2 \times 2 = 4\) g). So the mass ratio of oxygen (anode) to hydrogen (cathode) is \(32 : 4 = 8 : 1\). (By volume the ratio is \(1 : 2\), since twice as much hydrogen is formed.)

rows.stem: Name a plant growth hormone synthesized at the shoot tip. Explain its effect on the growth of a plant in response to light.
rows.solution:
Auxin is synthesised at the shoot tip.

When light falls on a plant from one side, auxin produced at the shoot tip diffuses towards the shaded side of the shoot.

The higher concentration of auxin on the shaded side stimulates the cells there to grow longer than the cells on the side exposed to light. So the shoot bends towards the light (phototropism).

rows.stem:
A 2000 W heater has a resistance of about \(25\,\Omega\), whereas a 100 W bulb has a resistance of \(500\,\Omega\). When 220 V is applied on these, then which of the two

(a) can carry large currents ?

(b) may be used with an electrical circuit having \(1{\cdot}0\) A rating ?

(c) will be fitted with a 15 A electric board and not with a 5 A electric board ?

Justify your answer in each case.
rows.solution:
For each appliance the current is \(I = \dfrac{P}{V}\) at \(V = 220\) V.

Heater: \(I_1 = \dfrac{2000}{220} = 9{\cdot}09\) A.

Bulb: \(I_2 = \dfrac{100}{220} = 0{\cdot}45\) A.

(Using \(I = \dfrac{V}{R}\) with the given resistances gives \(\dfrac{220}{25} = 8{\cdot}8\) A and \(\dfrac{220}{500} = 0{\cdot}44\) A; the heater's resistance is only "about" \(25\,\Omega\), and both routes lead to the same answers.)

(a) The 2000 W heater can carry large currents: it draws about 9 A, far more than the bulb's \(0{\cdot}45\) A.

(b) The 100 W bulb may be used in a circuit rated \(1{\cdot}0\) A, since it draws only \(0{\cdot}45\) A, which is less than 1 A. The heater would draw far more than the rating.

(c) The 2000 W heater is fitted to a 15 A board and not a 5 A board, since the current it draws, \(9{\cdot}09\) A, is more than 5 A but less than 15 A.

rows.stem:
(i) Which type of circuits — series or parallel, should be used when you have to operate different electrical gadgets in your house ? List two reasons for your answer.

(ii) Find the current flowing through the following electric circuit :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (ii) gives the circuit only as a drawing: a 3 ohm resistor, then two branches in parallel (one a single 6 ohm resistor, the other two 6 ohm resistors in series), then a second 3 ohm resistor, all in series with a 4.5 V battery and a plug key. Page idx 22.
rows.solution:
(i) A parallel circuit should be used. Any two reasons:

1. Each appliance has its own switch, so it can be turned on and off separately.

2. If one appliance stops working or is switched off, the others remain unaffected.

3. Each appliance gets the full (same) potential difference and draws the current it needs.

4. The total resistance of a parallel circuit is less than the smallest resistance in it.

(ii) The two \(6\,\Omega\) resistors in series in the lower branch have a combined resistance

\(R_1 = 6 + 6 = 12\,\Omega\).

This branch is in parallel with the single \(6\,\Omega\) resistor, so their combined resistance \(R_2\) is given by

\(\dfrac{1}{R_2} = \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{2 + 1}{12} = \dfrac{1}{4}\), so \(R_2 = 4\,\Omega\).

The parallel group is in series with the two \(3\,\Omega\) resistors, so the total resistance is

\(R = 3 + 4 + 3 = 10\,\Omega\).

Current \(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{4{\cdot}5}{10} = 0{\cdot}45\) A.

(The marking scheme prints the sum \(\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{12}\) as \(\dfrac{9}{20}\); it is \(\dfrac{3}{12} = \dfrac{1}{4}\), which is what gives the scheme's own \(4{\cdot}0\,\Omega\).)

rows.stem:
The values of current I flowing in a given resistor for the corresponding values of potential difference V across the resistor are given in the following table :

| I (Amperes) | \(0{\cdot}5\) | \(1{\cdot}0\) | \(2{\cdot}0\) | \(3{\cdot}0\) | \(3{\cdot}5\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V (Volts) | \(1{\cdot}5\) | \(3{\cdot}0\) | \(6{\cdot}2\) | \(9{\cdot}3\) | \(10{\cdot}8\) |

(i) Plot a graph between V and I.

(ii) Calculate the resistance of the resistor with the help of the graph.

(iii) What does the graph represent ?

(iv) Why should this graph pass through the origin ?
rows.solution:
(i) Take the current I along the x-axis and the potential difference V along the y-axis, with a scale such as 1 cm \(= 0{\cdot}5\) A and 1 cm \(= 1\) V. Plot the points \((0{\cdot}5, 1{\cdot}5)\), \((1{\cdot}0, 3{\cdot}0)\), \((2{\cdot}0, 6{\cdot}2)\), \((3{\cdot}0, 9{\cdot}3)\) and \((3{\cdot}5, 10{\cdot}8)\), and draw the best straight line through them, passing through the origin.

(ii) The resistance is the slope of the V-I graph. Take two points on the line, for example \(I_1 = 2{\cdot}0\) A, \(V_1 = 6{\cdot}2\) V and \(I_2 = 3{\cdot}0\) A, \(V_2 = 9{\cdot}3\) V:

\(R = \dfrac{V_2 - V_1}{I_2 - I_1} = \dfrac{9{\cdot}3 - 6{\cdot}2}{3{\cdot}0 - 2{\cdot}0} = \dfrac{3{\cdot}1}{1{\cdot}0} = 3{\cdot}1\,\Omega\).

(Readings from a hand-drawn line vary a little; any pair of well-separated points gives about \(3{\cdot}1\,\Omega\).)

(iii) The graph is a straight line through the origin, so V is directly proportional to I: the resistor obeys Ohm's law, and its resistance remains constant.

(iv) When the potential difference across the resistor is zero, no current flows through it: \(I = 0\) when \(V = 0\). So the graph must pass through the origin.
